effects.log: You promise. {npc} writes it in the ledger and tilts it toward you to check the spelling.

choices.text: Say the house may send its warden-gods as it likes, and meet {him}

ok.log: {npc} rises from the flagstones, shakes out {his} sleeves, and laughs. "They said you would," {he} says. "I am to say it was well done."

fail.log: {npc} receives your strike in the palm and returns it through the elbow. The court is very quiet while you stand up.

choices.text: Offer the house a tithe of your offerings to keep it

effects.log: You name the share. {npc} tallies it, and the house grudgingly accepts. You will be reminded each festival.

events.text: A herald arrives at your sanctum with a bronze plaque, unwrapped, bearing the first stanza of the {bb_art} and the seal of {bb_house}. {npc}, who carries it, is clearly uneasy. The plaque, {he} says, is the house's formal question. The question is simple. What will you do with the plaque? Behind {him} incense curls quietly.

choices.text: Hang the plaque in your shrine and keep the art quiet

effects.log: You hang it. {npc} bows, relieved, and is gone before the incense burns down.

choices.text: Hand the plaque back through the doorway, edge first

ok.log: {npc} catches it, staggers, and sets it down with care. "A fair answer," {he} says, "and a bad bruise."

fail.log: {npc} catches the plaque and uses it to turn your wrist. You discover the sanctum floor, and the plaque set gently by your head.

choices.text: Offer the house a long season of prayers in its name

effects.log: You promise a season of rites. The house accepts the promise, and the bill for the incense.

events.text: At the gate of your temple, in the mid-morning crowd, {npc} unrolls a white banner on a short pole, the old form of reminder. "Third asking," {he} says clearly, for the faithful to hear. "The {bb_art} is the blood's of {bb_house}. You have wielded it before other pantheons. Let it be decided here, in the open, before the gods who watch."

choices.text: Take the pole from {him} and accept the reminder

ok.log: {npc} yields at last, and the crowd lets out its breath. The banner comes down quietly, folded in four.

fail.log: {npc} stops the pole with a forearm and takes your guard. The crowd murmurs. The banner goes up again.

choices.text: Put the art away, aloud, before the faithful

effects.log: You say it clear and low. The crowd settles. {npc} lowers the banner, and bows with a shade of sorrow.

events.text: A prayer slip, folded small, lies on your altar among the offerings. It bears three lines in a hand you taught. The {bb_art} was never meant to be locked, {npc} writes, and {he} has gone to learn what happens when it isn't. The elders of {bb_house} are in the antechamber, unusually silent, keeping their hands inside their sleeves.

choices.text: Send your people after them

effects.log: You fold the slip and give it to the nearest elder, and the order with it. You wanted to sit down, afterward, and did not.

choices.text: Go after them yourself

ok.log: You find {npc} in a hill-shrine mending a pilgrim's sandal. {He} puts it down. You sit on the step until dusk, and {he} follows you home in the morning.

fail.log: You find {npc} in a hill-shrine mending a sandal. {He} listens, thanks you, and goes on mending. You walk home with the question of the elders still on your shoulders.

choices.text: Let them go, and lift the binding

effects.log: You burn the slip at the altar. When the elders ask, you tell them the line has been struck, and mean it.

events.text: A river-god, passing through your domain with a boat of reeds, mentions that a young traveller on the river last month performed an art never seen in these waters, flawlessly, to dry a stranded child's clothes. The river-god shows you the gesture. It is the {bb_art}. It is {npc}, gone since the first thaw, and the elders of {bb_house} knew but you.

choices.text: Send your people after them

effects.log: You thank the river-god and send for the ones whose business this is. The boat is gone before you have finished.

choices.text: Go after them yourself

ok.log: You find {npc} at a river-shrine at dusk, asleep on a pile of reeds. {He} wakes, and the years fall off {him}. You walk back together, and say little.

fail.log: You find {npc} at a river-shrine at dusk, awake and unrepentant. {He} hears you out, makes tea, and goes on watching the water. You walk home alone.

choices.text: Let them go, and lift the binding

effects.log: You send the river-god off with a good offering. At the next dawn you strike the line from the Book yourself. It is harder than the binding was.

events.text: At the school's autumn muster, with the harvest carts still rattling in the lane, you stand on the teaching-stool and say it: the {bb_art} of {bb_house} is not taught to outsiders, nor carried off by those who leave. A boy at the back, ink on his cuffs, asks whether it may at least be written down. The senior pupils lean in, not breathing.

choices.text: Tell the boy it will be written once, and kept under lock

effects.log: He nods, solemn as a magistrate. The ledger-lock is oiled that evening.

choices.text: Say that what is written can be copied, and what is learned cannot

effects.log: It is a harder answer than he wanted. Lessons resume at dawn, quieter.

events.text: An old uncle of the house brings the family tally-stick down from the rafters, the one notched for every generation, and asks you to cut the next notch for the {bb_art}. It is to belong to {bb_house} by blood, and by nothing else. Aunts crowd the doorway with flour on their arms. The knife is old and very sharp. "Your name goes on the wood," he says.

choices.text: Cut the notch cleanly, and hand back the stick

effects.log: The notch is straight. The old man runs a thumb along it, nods, and hangs the stick up again.

choices.text: Ask what the previous notch was for

effects.log: He tells you. It was a well, dug in a bad year. You had not known it was a well.

events.text: The lesser houses that hold land under {bb_house} send their stewards to the capital for it, since a throne's line needs witnesses. They stand in the long audience room in their mud-stiff court shoes and hear that the {bb_art} is the royal blood's, and lent to them only while they keep faith. In the corridor afterwards their murmuring is careful and sad.

choices.text: Walk the corridor among them, and let yourself be seen

effects.log: You walk it slowly. Talk stops where you pass and starts again behind you. That is what you came for.

choices.text: Send wine to their lodgings and stay in the palace

effects.log: They drink it. By morning they have decided it was the chancellor's idea, which suits everyone.

events.text: The notice goes up on the kitchen door beside the rota for water-carrying: the {bb_art} is the property of the blood of {bb_house}. Those who know it may keep it. Those who leave may not show it on any road. The scullion beside you stops scraping the pot. You know the {bb_art}. Everyone in the yard has just remembered that you do.

choices.text: Nod to the scullion and finish your bowl

effects.log: It costs nothing today. You file the day away for later.

choices.text: Ask the steward aloud what happens to one who forgets

effects.log: The yard goes still. "A cousin calls, and asks them to remember," the steward says, scraping a pot of his own. "It is a short visit. They have had practice."

events.text: The bailiff of {bb_house} finds you in the guest cottage and tells you himself, which is the courtesy, with two farmhands waiting at the gate, which is the point. The {bb_art} is the house's blood from today. You learned it at their hearth. Nobody asks it back. They only want you to know that you are not family, and that the ferry-men have been told.

choices.text: Thank the bailiff for coming in person

effects.log: You thank him. He looks a little disappointed, a second speech ready, and tucks it back into his coat.

choices.text: Ask whose notion this was

effects.log: He smiles, says nothing, and that is how you learn it was someone who has watched you for years.

events.text: {npc} takes the chair across your kitchen table without being asked and sets down a torn corner of the house's account-book. On it are the {bb_art}, the name of {bb_house}, and, in small writing, yours. "You were at the hearth when it was fixed," {he} says, kindly enough. "You went. Now people have seen it in a market. The family would like that to end."

choices.text: Agree to keep it to yourself from now on

effects.log: You give your word over the table. {npc} slides the scrap across so that you may keep it, and finishes your bread.

choices.text: Say {he} is welcome to try to take it

ok.log: {npc} climbs up off your floor, chuckling and bruised. "They said you would," {he} says. "They will send me back."

fail.log: {npc} lifts you by the coat, sets you gently against the dresser, and goes on talking as though you had never moved.

choices.text: Offer to pay for everything the house taught you

effects.log: You count it out in neat stacks. {npc} counts it again, writes a receipt on a corn-husk, and crosses your name off. It is the politest thing that has ever happened to you.

events.text: You know the gait from the lane before you see the face; every child of {bb_house} has the same rolling step from carrying water up the hill. {npc} stops ten paces from your orchard gate and says the line {he} has said elsewhere. "The {bb_art} is the family's, and you are not. Keep it in your head if you must. Not in your hands."

choices.text: Say you will put it away for now

effects.log: You nod. {npc} nods back and stays put until you have gone round {him}. The lane is long after that.

choices.text: Show {him} what your hands remember

ok.log: {npc} ends up in the hedge and laughs once, short. "You were always good," {he} says. "It was never about that."

fail.log: {npc} has the rolling step for a reason. You learn why on the cold ground, with {his} boot on your wrist and a thrush singing close by.

choices.text: Ask what the family would take to let it be

effects.log: "More than you think," says {npc}, and names it. It is exactly what you have laid by. They have always kept very good tally-sticks.

events.text: No torn page this time, no cousin's courtesy. {npc} walks in the front way at midday while the neighbours are drawing water. "You were asked three times," {he} says, loud enough to carry to the well. "You used the {bb_art} again. {bb_house} sends its good wishes, and me."

choices.text: Meet {him} in the lane, in front of them all

ok.log: {npc} goes down before the same neighbours {he} meant to impress. You almost pity {him}. They will have to enter that in the family book too.

fail.log: You go down before the same neighbours you were hiding it from. {npc} waits until you can breathe, and tells you once more in case you missed it.

choices.text: Put it away, and say so where the well-line can hear

effects.log: You say it clearly. It costs more than a fight would. {npc} bows, and the well-line goes back to its buckets.

events.text: The latch is up and you did not lift it. {npc} sits by your stove with your own kettle on, in the chair that watches the door. "More will come after me, if I do not settle this," {he} says. "I would rather not be followed. You could see to that, or I could. Finish your supper. {bb_house} has waited through harder winters."

choices.text: Finish the supper, then finish this

ok.log: You overturn the table and a good deal else. {npc} leaves by the shutter and sends a most correct note about the stew.

fail.log: {npc} breaks nothing but you. {He} washes the bowl before going.

choices.text: Ask what {he} wants, and what the house wants

effects.log: It is large and {he} has it written down. You pay. {He} seems sorry to go, and takes the spoon along.

events.text: The quilt has been folded in thirds, very neatly, and {npc} is not under it. A note on the pillow, in a hand you taught: no apology. The {bb_art} was given to {him} before it was ever fixed to the blood, and {he} means to see what else the world is hiding. The elders of {bb_house} are waiting in your yard. They have not yet crossed the step.

choices.text: Send your people after them

effects.log: You open the door and give the order. Nobody asks if you are sure. You half hoped someone would.

choices.text: Go after them yourself

ok.log: You catch up with {npc} at the second ferry. You talk till the boat has gone twice. {He} comes home, not because you were right but because you came.

fail.log: You catch up at the second ferry. You say all of it. {He} hears you out and boards, and you stand on the landing with the elders' question still unanswered.

choices.text: Let them go, and lift the binding

effects.log: You open the door and say it to their faces. The arguing lasts a month. Somewhere on the road, {npc} never learns how close it was.

events.text: A drover mentions it over the price of lamp-oil: on the north road a young stranger is working for coin in a manner seen in only one family. The drover describes the {bb_art} quite well, with no idea whose table this is. It is {npc}, gone since the thaw, and everyone in {bb_house} knew but you.

choices.text: Send your people after them

effects.log: You finish the talk of oil and see the drover out. Then you send for those whose business this is.

choices.text: Go after them yourself

ok.log: You find {npc} in the third town you try, lip split, counting winnings. {He} looks up and is suddenly very young. You walk home together and never mention it.

fail.log: You find {npc} in the third town you try. {He} is doing well. {He} buys you tea, the worst you have had, and you walk home alone.

choices.text: Let them go, and lift the binding

effects.log: You send the drover off with a fair price on the oil. Next morning you strike the line from the book yourself. It is harder than the binding was.

events.text: Two old stewards of the ancestral hall have walked a long road to stand in your yard and not quite look at you. The head of the house is weary, they say, though some still speak warmly of your line. The boards have been asked, and the seal is yours if you will have it: the lands, the feuds, the ledgers, everything that comes with the name. They will wait, but not for long.

choices.text: Take the seal

effects.log: You say yes. They bow lower than expected, and then, sooner than expected, start telling you what is wrong.

choices.text: Not now. Let the head keep the seat

effects.log: They do not argue. They drink the tea, look around at what you have instead, and go. They will ask again in ten years, if anyone is left to ask.

events.text: The letter is in the old form, on the house's own paper, sealed in the colour used only on days of mourning. The head of your blood will step aside, if you come. The elders have counted heads and you are the one they can bear. You read it three times. It does not say what becomes of what you built here. It does not need to: a house takes all of you.

choices.text: Go home and take the seat

effects.log: You answer the same day. There are things you will miss. You learn what they are later, one at a time.

choices.text: Send it back, with respect

effects.log: You return it with your respect and a very fine gift. The elders will keep the gift, and write again in ten years.

events.text: The school of {bb_house} keeps its secrets in a rice-jar, literally: the pupils drop a folded slip into it on the day they first learn the {bb_art}. Today you are asked to read the slips aloud, one by one, and rebind each pupil to the house. Some slips are tidy. Some are smeared with tears. A thin girl in the front row stares at the jar as if it might bite.

choices.text: Read every slip, and let each pupil hear their own

effects.log: It takes the whole morning. Afterwards no one leaves, and no one speaks.

choices.text: Hand the jar back and say each must read their own

effects.log: The pupils take turns. The thin girl goes last, and her voice carries to the gate.

events.text: A herald from {bb_house} rides through the market town ringing a handbell and shouting a single sentence: the {bb_art} belongs to the blood. He says it three times in the square, and once under your window. Baskets are set down. Hawkers go quiet. You know the {bb_art}. A woman at the cheese-stall looks at your hands and then pointedly away.

choices.text: Buy a wedge of cheese and walk on

effects.log: The woman wraps it quickly. You eat it on the bridge, and think.

choices.text: Follow the herald to the end of the street and ask what it means

effects.log: He tells you, weary and plain. It is much shorter than the shouting.

events.text: {npc} appears at the threshing-floor at dusk, a lean hired hand of {bb_house}, with a straw in {his} teeth. "A carter saw you use the {bb_art} on the bridge," {he} says, spitting the straw. "Plain as day, in front of half the market. The family would like to know if they ought to send someone to talk, or someone to be firm."

choices.text: Promise to be careful on the roads

effects.log: You promise. {npc} nods and sets off, whistling, as though the matter had been a favour.

choices.text: Tell {him} to be as firm as {he} likes

ok.log: {npc} gets up from the chaff, blowing, and grins. "They said you would," {he} says. "I am to tell them it was a clean fight."

fail.log: {npc} holds you by the collar for a count of ten, kindly, then lets go. The chaff is in your hair all week.

choices.text: Offer a sum for the right to keep using it

effects.log: You name a figure. {npc} turns it over, nods, and writes it on {his} palm with a bit of charcoal. "They will take it," {he} says, "and think less of you for asking."

events.text: A folded cloth arrives by the post-rider, tied with the colours of {bb_house}. In it is a single wooden button carved with the first line of the {bb_art}. {npc} arrives an hour afterwards, hat in hand. The button, {he} explains, is how the family asks. The question is what you will do with the button. The post-rider has not left, and is pretending to water the horse.

choices.text: Send the button back, and promise to keep the art quiet

effects.log: You wrap it again. {npc} sighs with relief, and takes the post-rider away with {him}.

choices.text: Press the button into {his} palm, and strike

ok.log: {npc} stares at the button, and at the ground. "A fair answer," {he} says, rising, "and a poor bruise."

fail.log: {npc} pockets the button and takes your arm into a lock so neat you do not notice until later. The post-rider applauds.

choices.text: Return the button with a purse of silver and a letter

effects.log: The purse is accepted. The letter is not answered, and you spend a year wondering how it was read.

events.text: A white sash is tied to your gate, the old signal in this country for a formal reminder. {npc} stands under it, hands visible. "Three times asked," {he} says. "I come as the fourth, which is the end of asking. The {bb_art} is the blood's of {bb_house}. The village may watch. Let us settle it on the green, as it was settled in my grandfather's day."

choices.text: Untie the sash and begin on the green

ok.log: {npc} yields, breathing hard, and takes the sash away. The village applauds in embarrassed silence.

fail.log: {npc} knots the sash round your wrist and gives it a small tug. "Remember this," {he} says, and withdraws.

choices.text: Put the art away aloud, before the village

effects.log: You say it clear and low. The green exhales. {npc} unties the sash from the gate and bows.

events.text: A paper boat is floating in the water-butt by your door. Unfolded, it is a letter in a hand you taught: the {bb_art} was never meant to be shut in a jar, {npc} writes, and {he} has gone to see what happens when it is let out. The elders of {bb_house} are already in the doorway, hats in their hands, unusually quiet.

choices.text: Send your people after them

effects.log: You pass the letter to the nearest elder, and the order with it. You wanted to sit down afterwards, and did not.

choices.text: Go after them yourself

ok.log: You find {npc} in a hill-hamlet mending a neighbour's roof. {He} puts down the hammer. You sit on the ridge until dusk. {He} follows you home next morning.

fail.log: You find {npc} in a hill-hamlet mending a roof. {He} hears you out, thanks you, and goes on mending. You walk home with the elders' question still on your shoulders.

choices.text: Let them go, and lift the binding

effects.log: You burn the letter in the stove. When the elders ask, you tell them the line has been struck, and mean it.

events.text: A fishwife on the river-quay, gutting carp, says casually that a young traveller on a barge last month was strikingly good at some art never seen on this river. The fishwife makes the gesture with a gutting knife. It is the {bb_art}, flawless. It is {npc}, gone since the plum-rains, and everyone in {bb_house} knew but you.

choices.text: Send your people after them

effects.log: You buy a carp you do not want and send for those whose business this is.

choices.text: Go after them yourself

ok.log: You find {npc} on the barge between two towns, sunburnt and cheerful. {He} sees you, and the cheer falls away. You talk until the barge has docked twice, and go home together.

fail.log: You find {npc} on the barge, sunburnt and cheerful. {He} hears you out, shakes {his} head kindly, and stays aboard. You watch the barge out of sight.

choices.text: Let them go, and lift the binding

effects.log: You tip the fishwife and tell the elders nothing. That night you strike the line from the book yourself, and it is harder than the binding was.
